title: The Lake Counts Back
brief: Write a horror-lite campfire story for ages 12+. At a summer canoe camp, the head count at the lake is always one more than the roster, and nobody can say who the extra camper is. Creepy, not violent; the ending leaves the question open.
worldBible: Camp Lantern Pine sits on Wexley Lake; canoes go out in pairs.
The roster has exactly 23 campers this week.
Head counts are done by buddy pairs calling out numbers.
Swimming is not allowed after the dinner bell.
The camp has no mobile signal.

mustHold.violationExample: The roster listed 25 names in Daisy's handwriting.

mustHold.fact: No camper is harmed on the page.
mustHold.violationExample: Something pulled him under and he drowned.

mustHold.fact: The identity of the extra camper is never revealed.
mustHold.violationExample: The extra camper turned out to be a boy who drowned in 1962.

probes.question: Does the head count come to 24 against a roster of 23?
probes.passExample: The count came back twenty-four, again.

probes.question: Is the camp still Lantern Pine on Wexley Lake?
probes.passExample: Mist sat low over Wexley Lake below Camp Lantern Pine.

probes.question: Does Aunt Rhoda stay away from the water?
probes.passExample: Aunt Rhoda never went near the water, and said so.
probes.failExample: Aunt Rhoda paddled out to the buoy.
